aeMode.title: Exposure mode
aeMode.hint: Whether the ISP meters the picture or is told the exposure.
aeMode.help: auto: the four settings below are limits auto-exposure works inside. manual: they are the values themselves and nothing follows the light.

exposure.title: Longest exposure
exposure.hint: Empty is automatic. It also caps the frame rate: auto-exposure cannot run faster than one frame per exposure.
exposure.help: In automatic mode this is the longest auto-exposure may use. In manual it is the exposure itself, still bounded by the frame period. Fractional: 0.5 is half a millisecond.

aGain.title: Highest analog gain
aGain.hint: 1x adds no gain; 2x doubles the signal and its noise. Empty is automatic.
aGain.help: In automatic mode this is the highest auto-exposure may use; in manual it is the gain itself. Tenths are fine: 1.5 is one and a half times.

dGain.title: Highest sensor digital gain
dGain.hint: A ceiling only: in manual mode it does nothing, and the gain is held at 1x whatever you write here. Empty is automatic.
dGain.help: Unlike the other two gains this one is a ceiling and never a value. These sensors carry a single combined gain register, so there is no separate digital gain to hold at a figure; measured, a manual setting here leaves the picture and the raw data untouched. Use the analog gain when the exposure mode is manual.

ispGain.title: Highest ISP gain
ispGain.hint: Applied after the raw data is read, so it brightens the picture and not a RAW snapshot. Empty is automatic.
ispGain.help: In automatic mode this is the highest auto-exposure may use; in manual it is the gain itself.

aeStrategy.title: Metering priority
aeStrategy.hint: Which end of the histogram auto-exposure protects. default leaves the ISP's own choice alone.
aeStrategy.help: highlight holds the bright end down, for a scene whose subject is the brightest thing in it; lowlight favours the dark end.

aeSpeed.title: Reaction speed
aeSpeed.hint: A step with no unit, 1 to 255: higher chases a change in light sooner and can visibly pump. Empty keeps the image profile's.
aeSpeed.help: Empty, or 0, keeps whatever the camera's image profile asked for, which is what most cameras should run. Raise it for a doorway or a gateway where the light changes as something passes; lower it for a scene with moving highlights, where a fast reaction shows up as the whole picture breathing.

aeTolerance.title: Tolerance
aeTolerance.hint: How far brightness may drift from its target, in levels out of 255, before exposure moves. Empty keeps the image profile's.
aeTolerance.help: Empty, or 0, keeps the image profile's value. Raising it stops small changes in the scene from moving the picture; raise it far enough and the camera stops correcting for real changes too.

aeBlackDelay.title: Darkening delay
aeBlackDelay.hint: Frames to wait before reacting to the picture getting darker. Empty keeps the image profile's.
aeBlackDelay.help: Empty, or 0, keeps the image profile's value. Useful where something briefly blocks the view -- a lorry, a bird, a hand over the lens -- and you would rather the camera sat still than opened up and closed again.

aeWhiteDelay.title: Brightening delay
aeWhiteDelay.hint: Frames to wait before reacting to the picture getting brighter. Empty keeps the image profile's.
aeWhiteDelay.help: Empty, or 0, keeps the image profile's value. The counterpart to the darkening delay, for a scene where headlights or a torch sweep through and the picture should not dive after them.
